title: Activate authenticator app
purpose: Enroll a time-based authenticator for future sign-in verification.
summary: Set up an authenticator app as a second step when you sign in to your own account.

tasks.title: Set up the authenticator app
steps: Scan the QR code with your authenticator app, or enter the [[Authenticator secret]] by hand.
Type the current six-digit code from the app in [[Authenticator code]].
Select [[Activate]]. The first time, ten recovery codes are created and shown next.

tasks.title: Give up the setup
steps: Leave with the normal account navigation. Nothing is activated until you select Activate.

good_to_know: Reloading this page creates new setup details. Use the QR code shown now.
Setup is blocked while any email address on your account is unverified.
Keep the recovery codes somewhere private. They let you sign in if you lose the app.
An authenticator app does not change your laboratory roles.

items.label: QR code
items.description: Scan into your authenticator app. Enrollment information belongs only to this signed-in account.

items.label: Authenticator secret
items.description: Disabled read-only enrollment secret beneath the QR image; use it for manual app setup or private recovery of the app configuration.

items.label: Authenticator code
items.description: Required current six-digit code from the new app. Default time steps are 30 seconds with no adjacent-step tolerance. A wrong or rate-limited code leaves activation incomplete.

items.label: Activate
items.description: Validates the code and creates the TOTP authenticator. If recovery codes do not exist, creates ten eight-digit recovery codes automatically and opens that page; otherwise returns to the MFA overview.

sections.title: Prerequisites and changing enrollment
paragraphs: Requires sign-in, recent reauthentication and no unverified associated email records. This check is not a blanket requirement that a verified email record must exist: an account with no address records passes that particular test. If an app is already active, this route opens deactivation instead. Reloading an unsubmitted activation form generates new enrollment information; use the QR/secret currently displayed. There is no Back or Cancel button in this form; leave through the normal account navigation to abandon enrollment.
